gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the same Algorithm 2 defect: the target d is an angular principal-angle deviation whose extremal scale is arccos(1/sqrt(n)), but both algorithm predicates compare it against the incompatible scalar scale 1/sqrt(n). It explicitly explains the resulting false rejection of exact extremal inputs and acceptance of nonextremal values, and prescribes recentering both thresholds at the angular value.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Algorithm 2 uses 1/sqrt(n) as the comparison threshold even though d is measured on the angular scale and the conjectured extremal value is arccos(1/sqrt(n)); consequently both the counterexample and extremal-candidate tests are misclassified.

component_coverage.gold_component: The value d and both Algorithm 2 predicates are centered on the wrong scale: d is an angular deviation with extremal value arccos(1/sqrt(n)), while the tests use 1/sqrt(n), causing exact extremal inputs to be rejected and nonextremal values potentially accepted.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies d as the largest-principal-angle deviation, states the angular extremal value, contrasts it with the thresholds 1/sqrt(n), derives the false-negative and false-positive behavior of the two branches, and gives the specific corrected angular thresholds.
